cases.sentence: Она пошла и рассказала ___, а он сказал:
cases.explain: «Божьему человеку» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Then she came and told the man of God. He said, “Go, sell the oil, and pay your debt; and you and your sons live on the rest.”

cases.sentence: Там жила одна ___, которая уговорила его остаться поесть.
cases.explain: «богатая женщина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: One day Elisha went to Shunem, where there was a prominent woman; and she persuaded him to eat bread. So it was, that as often as he passed by, he turned in there to eat bread.

cases.sentence: Она отправилась в путь и пришла к ___ на гору Кармил.
cases.explain: «Божьему человеку» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: So she went, and came to the man of God to Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her afar off, he said to Gehazi his servant, “Behold, there is the Shunammite.

cases.sentence: Когда же она пришла к ___ на гору, она обняла его ноги.
cases.explain: «Божьему человеку» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: When she came to the man of God to the hill, she caught hold of his feet. Gehazi came near to thrust her away; but the man of God said, “Leave her alone; for her soul is troubled within her; and Yahweh has hidden it from me, and has not told me.”

cases.sentence: Один из них вышел в поле собирать овощи и нашел ___.
cases.explain: «дикие огурцы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: One went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine, and gathered a lap full of wild gourds from it, and came and cut them up into the pot of stew; for they didn’t recognize them.

cases.sentence: Он набрал полную одежду ___ с него и, когда вернулся, накрошил их в котел с похлебкой, хотя никто не знал, что это такое.
cases.explain: «диких плодов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: One went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine, and gathered a lap full of wild gourds from it, and came and cut them up into the pot of stew; for they didn’t recognize them.

cases.sentence: Из Баал-Шалиши пришел некий человек, который принес ___ двадцать ячменных хлебов, испеченных из зерна первого урожая, и колосья с молодым зерном.
cases.explain: «Божьему человеку» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: A man from Baal Shalishah came, and brought the man of God some bread of the first fruits: twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. He said, “Give to the people, that they may eat.”

cases.sentence: Из Баал-Шалиши пришел некий человек, который принес Божьему человеку двадцать ___, испеченных из зерна первого урожая, и колосья с молодым зерном.
cases.explain: «ячменных хлебов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: A man from Baal Shalishah came, and brought the man of God some bread of the first fruits: twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. He said, “Give to the people, that they may eat.”

cases.sentence: Из Баал-Шалиши пришел некий человек, который принес Божьему человеку двадцать ячменных хлебов, испеченных из зерна ___, и колосья с молодым зерном.
cases.explain: «первого урожая» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: A man from Baal Shalishah came, and brought the man of God some bread of the first fruits: twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. He said, “Give to the people, that they may eat.”

cases.sentence: Из Баал-Шалиши пришел некий человек, который принес Божьему человеку двадцать ячменных хлебов, испеченных из зерна первого урожая, и колосья с ___.
cases.explain: «молодым зерном» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: A man from Baal Shalishah came, and brought the man of God some bread of the first fruits: twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. He said, “Give to the people, that they may eat.”
